title: Burkholder Martingale Transform Inequality
abstract: Formalizes Burkholder's sharp Lp inequality for real-valued martingale transforms: if `f` is a discrete martingale and `w` a predictable multiplier bounded by `1`, then the Lp norm of the transform `w ⋆ₘ f` is at most `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f`, where `pStar p` is the maximum of `p` and its conjugate exponent. The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).

informal.MeasureTheory.Lp_Burkholder_inequality_m: The sharp Lp Burkholder inequality: for a discrete martingale `f` and a predictable multiplier `w` with `|w n| ≤ 1`, the Lp norm of the martingale transform `(w ⋆ₘ f) n` is bounded by `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f n`.
informal.MeasureTheory.martingaleTransform_martin: The martingale transform of a martingale by a strongly predictable bounded multiplier is itself a martingale.
informal.Majorants.exists_majorant_p_g_1: For every exponent `p > 1` there exists a Burkholder majorant, the special function dominating the payoff and driving the inequality.
